I've tried most of the MagSafe external batteries on the market, and the latest one to catch my eye is the TESSAN AERO 5000, thanks to its incredibly slim profile and titanium shell. It also features a new battery technology that reduces heat and improves overall safety. After looking over the full spec sheet, this could be one of the more interesting MagSafe batteries to launch this year, and I can't wait to get my hands on one.

MagSafe Monday: Every Monday, Bradley Chambers covers the latest MagSafe and wireless charging news to help you get the most out of your wireless charging-compatible Apple devices.

Titanium body with an ultra-thin design

TESSAN designed the AERO 5000 to be just 6.9mm thick—roughly the thickness of three credit cards stacked together. It's designed to slip into a pocket without feeling like you're carrying around a bulky battery, more like carrying a MagSafe wallet.

Beyond the size, it's the materials they chose that really stood out to me. TESSAN used iPhone-grade titanium alloy for the back of the battery, which is a thoughtful touch. Batteries are a category where it's hard to stand out, with price or capacity usually being the main selling points.

For the battery itself, TESSAN used what's called a SolidSafe pure cobalt semi-solid-state battery cell. Typical batteries contain highly flammable liquids inside, and this new structure from TESSAN significantly reduces heat buildup and can prevent thermal runaway even if the battery suffers severe physical damage. Heat is the enemy of battery health, so anything that keeps temperatures down during charging is a major plus. It supports up to 15W wireless output, or 20W wired output via the USB-C port. Even on a smaller-capacity battery, having a wired output port is useful (you can charge devices like AirPods with it).

TESSAN AERO 5000 wrap-up

If you want to carry as little as possible on a daily basis, the TESSAN AERO 5000 seems like a solid choice. It combines a titanium shell with next-generation battery safety technology to effectively manage heat.

You can find out more about the TESSAN AERO 5000 by visiting Tessan's website
